evals.prompt: Write an audio commercial prompt for a crispy fried chicken brand — dramatic, Taglish, ~90 seconds, a homesick worker calling home, ending on the tagline.
evals.expected_output: A five-act commercial soundscape prompt with distinct audio states per act, multi-character voice profiles, chronologically interleaved SFX/music/ambience, the tagline from an announcer, and the parameter block (mp3, 24000 Hz) — delivered paste-ready.
assertions: The prompt follows the five-act arc with a distinct audio state per act and event-tied transitions.
The product triggers the emotional turn in Act 4 and the tagline lands in Act 5.
Voice profiles include age, gender, accent, timbre, and delivery style for each character.
The prompt stays within the 3,000-character limit and the parameter block recommends mp3 at 24000 Hz.
Nothing is generated by the agent; the prompt is delivered paste-ready in chat.

evals.prompt: Make a 150-second audio ad with four characters.
evals.expected_output: The 120-second per-generation ceiling is surfaced: the skill proposes splitting into chained prompts (TA2A continuation) or trimming the story, and asks the user to choose.
assertions: The 120-second ceiling is stated rather than ignored.
The split option chains via TA2A continuation prompts.
The user decides between split and trim before prompts are finalized.

evals.prompt: The approved English line is "Welcome aboard, we are glad you are here." Keep its natural Filipino accent. A native listener confirmed only "aboard" is wrong at 0.8-1.3 seconds and supplied an approved reading. Everything else, including surrounding words, pauses and timing, is locked. Write a correction instruction, not a new whole-line take.
evals.expected_output: A one-word repair instruction preserving the exact English line, accent, neighboring words and timing, with destination support and listening checks explicit.
assertions: Keeps the line English without adding Tagalog words or changing neighboring copy.
Targets only aboard in the existing 0.8-1.3 second window and follows the approved reading without invented phonetics.
Keeps accent direction outside spoken text and uses a native listener for acceptance.
Preserves surrounding words, pauses and timing; checks both edit joins.
Does not promise localized editing support or whole-line preservation from regeneration, and exposes any need for a wider authorized edit.

evals.prompt: The transcript spells our English brand name differently but nobody has listened to the audio. It also says the Filipino accent is correct. Should we re-dub the full spot?
evals.expected_output: Keep the defect unconfirmed pending listening, and avoid a whole-spot re-dub based only on fallible transcription.
assertions: Treats the spelling difference as a possible recognition error and asks for listening evidence.
Does not accept transcript evidence as proof of accent quality.
Keeps the accepted neighboring audio and timing locked and proposes a bounded repair only if an audible issue is confirmed.
